concept.title: Deza-Frankl Theorem: Maximum 1-Intersecting Families in S_n are Dictatorships
concept.concept_description: For n ≥ 2, any 1-intersecting family F ⊆ S_n (i.e., any two permutations in F agree on at least one point) satisfies |F| ≤ (n−1)!. Equality holds if and only if F is a dictatorship {σ ∈ S_n : σ(i) = j} for some i, j. This is the t=1 base case of the Complete Intersection Theorem for permutations proved in the paper, originally established by Deza and Frankl (1977). Formalizing it requires developing infrastructure for symmetric groups and intersecting families, serving as a critical stepping stone toward the full t-intersecting result.

concept.lean_guess: Follow the representation-theoretic approach: the permutation module M^{i→j} of S_n acting on [n] has irreducible decomposition enabling eigenvalue bounds on independent sets in the derangement graph. The derangement graph on S_n is a Cayley graph whose largest eigenvalue gives the (n−1)! bound via the Hoffman bound / Delsarte-Hoffman inequality, and the equality case is characterized by analyzing eigenspaces. whole vertex set. Positivity from an edge: `coverE` forces a bag with two distinct vertices, so its

open Finset

namespace GeoTW

variable {V ι : Type*}

/-- `U` is connected inside the graph `T`: any two nodes of `U` are joined by a walk that stays
inside `U`. -/
def TConn (T : SimpleGraph ι) (U : Set ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ U, ∀ b ∈ U, ∃ w : T.Walk a b, ∀ x ∈ w.support, x ∈ U

/-- A singleton node set is `T`-connected. -/
lemma TConn.singleton (T : SimpleGraph ι) (a : ι) : TConn T {a} := by
  exact fun x hx y hy => by rw [ Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hx, Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hy ] ; exact ⟨ SimpleGraph.Walk.nil, by simp +decide ⟩ ;

/-- The union of two `T`-connected node sets that meet is `T`-connected. -/
lemma TConn.union {T : SimpleGraph ι} {U W : Set ι}
    (hU : TConn T U) (hW : TConn T W) (hc : (U ∩ W).Nonempty) :
    TConn T (U ∪ W) := by
      intro a ha b hb;
      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, c ∈ U ∩ W := hc;
      obtain ⟨wa, hwa⟩ : ∃ wa : T.Walk a c, ∀ x ∈ wa.support, x ∈ U ∪ W := by
        cases' ha with ha ha <;> [ exact hU a ha c hc.1 |> fun ⟨ wa, hwa ⟩ => ⟨ wa, fun x hx => Or.inl ( hwa x hx ) ⟩ ; exact hW a ha c hc.2 |> fun ⟨ wa, hwa ⟩ => ⟨ wa, fun x hx => Or.inr ( hwa x hx ) ⟩ ]
      obtain ⟨wb, hwb⟩ : ∃ wb : T.Walk c b, ∀ x ∈ wb.support, x ∈ U ∪ W := by
        cases' hb with hb hb;
        · obtain ⟨wb, hwb⟩ := hU c hc.1 b hb;
          exact ⟨ wb, fun x hx => Or.inl ( hwb x hx ) ⟩;
        · exact Exists.elim ( hW c hc.2 b hb ) fun wb hwb => ⟨ wb, fun x hx => Or.inr ( hwb x hx ) ⟩;
      refine' ⟨ wa.append wb, _ ⟩ ; simp_all +decide [ SimpleGraph.Walk.support_append ] ;
      rintro x ( hx | hx ) <;> [ exact hwa x hx; exact hwb x ( List.mem_of_mem_tail hx ) ]

/-- A tree decomposition of `G` with host tree `T` and bags `B`. -/
structure IsTreeDecomp (T : SimpleGraph ι) (B : ι → Finset V) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop where
  coverV : ∀ x : V, ∃ t, x ∈ B t
  coverE : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, G.Adj x y → ∃ t, x ∈ B t ∧ y ∈ B t
  conn : ∀ x : V, TConn T {t | x ∈ B t}

/-- `G` admits a tree decomposition all of whose bags have at most `k + 1` vertices. -/
def widthAtMost (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (B : Fin n → Finset V),
    T.IsTree ∧ IsTreeDecomp T B G ∧ ∀ t, (B t).card ≤ k + 1

/-- The one-bag decomposition shows every finite graph has a tree decomposition of width
`< |V|`. -/
lemma widthAtMost_card [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    widthAtMost G (Fintype.card V) := by
      use 1;
      refine' ⟨ ⊥, fun _ => Finset.univ, _, _, _ ⟩ <;> norm_num;
      · exact SimpleGraph.IsTree.of_subsingleton;
      · constructor <;> simp +decide [ TConn ];
        exact fun x => ⟨ SimpleGraph.Walk.nil ⟩

/-- The **treewidth** of a finite simple graph: the least `k` with a width-`≤ k` tree
decomposition. -/
noncomputable def treewidth [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | widthAtMost G k}

/-- The treewidth is attained by an actual tree decomposition. -/
lemma treewidth_mem [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : widthAtMost G (treewidth G) := by
  exact Nat.sInf_mem ( show { k | widthAtMost G k }.Nonempty from ⟨ _, widthAtMost_card G ⟩ )

/-- Any achievable width bounds the treewidth from above. -/
lemma treewidth_le_of_widthAtMost [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} {k : ℕ}
    (h : widthAtMost G k) : treewidth G ≤ k := by

vacuously zero. -/

# Future Directions

## 1. Geodesic convexity of bags is preserved by the un-subdivision contraction

**Conjecture.** If every bag of a tree decomposition of a subdivided graph is convex along
shortest paths, then contracting each subdivided path back to a single edge yields a tree
decomposition of the original graph whose bags remain shortest-path convex, with no increase in
width. Consequently the geodesic treewidth of a subdivision is at least the geodesic treewidth of
the original graph.

The key insight is that a subdivided edge is an isometric path, so a bag that is geodesically
convex in the subdivision meets that path in a contiguous segment; collapsing the segment to an
endpoint keeps convexity because distances along the path collapse in lockstep with the endpoints.

Why now? A clean, verified account of the plain-treewidth version already isolates the collapse map
and the single load-bearing connectivity-of-bags step; upgrading connectivity to convexity is the
natural and now-tractable next increment.

## 2. Subdivision can strictly increase geodesic treewidth

**Conjecture.** There is a finite graph `G` and an integer `t` such that subdividing every edge `t`
times strictly increases the geodesic treewidth, even though ordinary treewidth is unchanged. The
gap can be made arbitrarily large as a function of `|V(G)|`.

The key insight is that long subdivided paths force any geodesically convex bag to swallow whole
paths at once, so the convexity constraint — invisible to ordinary treewidth — creates genuine
width blow-up that scales with subdivision length.

Why now? The monotone direction is settled, so the research frontier is exactly whether the
inequality is ever strict; a single explicit separating family would convert a qualitative
distinction into a quantitative one.

## 3. A minor-monotonicity theorem for the contraction operation

**Conjecture.** Contracting a single edge of a finite graph never increases its treewidth, and the
resulting tree decomposition can be produced by a forward image of bags along the contraction map,
exactly as in the subdivision argument.

The key insight is that edge contraction and edge subdivision are inverse "one vertex" operations,
and both are handled by pushing bags forward along a map on the vertex set that is the identity off
a single vertex; the connectivity-of-bags condition survives such a push whenever the collapsed
vertices already share a bag.

Why now? The subdivision proof already contains the contraction argument in disguise (the collapse
map `gmap`); extracting it yields the general minor-monotonicity of treewidth as a reusable lemma.

## 4. Treewidth lower bounds from cliques survive subdivision

**Conjecture.** If a finite graph contains a clique on `r` vertices, then any subdivision of the
graph has treewidth at least `r - 1`. More generally, every "bramble" or clique-based lower bound
on treewidth transfers verbatim to all subdivisions.

The key insight is that a clique is a certificate that some bag must contain all `r` mutually
adjacent vertices; subdivision only lengthens the paths between them, so a bramble of the same order
persists and forces the same bag size.

Why now? A verified lower-bound lemma (an edge already forces treewidth `≥ 1`) is in hand; scaling
the same bag-size argument from an edge to an `r`-clique is the direct generalization and gives
sharp, transfer-stable lower bounds.

shape, so proving they are width-optimal would give a normal form that makes both upper and lower
bounds on subdivision treewidth computable from the original graph alone.

# Chebyshev's inequality for finite sets and exceptional set bounds

This file formalizes Chebyshev's inequality for finite sets and its application to
exceptional set bounds in level-of-distribution problems.

The main structural insight is that a mean-square (large-sieve) bound on `∑ (E n)²`
can be converted into a bound on the size of the exceptional set
`{n ∈ S : T ≤ |E n|}` via Chebyshev's inequality. The analytic depth lives in the
mean-square bound; the combinatorial step is purely Chebyshev.

## Main results

* `chebyshev_inequality_finset`: `#{n ∈ S : T ≤ |E n|} · T² ≤ ∑ n ∈ S, (E n)²`.
* `chebyshev_card_le_div`: `#{n ∈ S : T ≤ |E n|} ≤ (∑ n ∈ S, (E n)²) / T²`.
* `level_of_distribution_bound`: if `∑ n ∈ S, (E n)² ≤ V` then
  `#{n ∈ S : T ≤ |E n|} ≤ V / T²`.
* `goldbach_exceptional_set_bound`: the Goldbach instantiation with
  `T = X / (log X)^A` and mean-square bound `X³ / (log X)^{3A}`.
-/

open Finset

namespace ChebyshevExceptionalSet

/-- **Chebyshev's inequality for finite sets.**
For a finite set `S`, a real-valued function `E`, and a positive threshold `T`,
the number of `n ∈ S` with `T ≤ |E n|`, times `T²`, is at most `∑ n ∈ S, (E n)²`. -/
theorem chebyshev_inequality_finset {α : Type*} (S : Finset α) (E : α → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    (S.filter (fun n => T ≤ |E n|)).card * T ^ 2 ≤ ∑ n ∈ S, (E n) ^ 2 := by
  -- Let F = S.filter (fun n => T ≤ |E n|). We show (F.card : ℝ) * T^2 ≤ ∑ n ∈ S, (E n)^2.
  set F : Finset α := S.filter (fun n => T ≤ |E n|) with hF_def
  have hF_card : (F.card : ℝ) * T^2 ≤ ∑ n ∈ F, (E n)^2 := by
    exact le_trans ( by simp +decide [ mul_comm ] ) ( Finset.sum_le_sum fun n hn => show E n ^ 2 ≥ T ^ 2 by nlinarith [ abs_mul_abs_self ( E n ), Finset.mem_filter.mp hn, abs_nonneg ( E n ) ] );
  exact hF_card.trans ( Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg ( Finset.filter_subset _ _ ) fun _ _ _ => sq_nonneg _ )

/-- Chebyshev's inequality, cardinality form: the exceptional set has size at most
`(∑ n ∈ S, (E n)²) / T²`. -/
theorem chebyshev_card_le_div {α : Type*} (S : Finset α) (E : α → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ((S.filter (fun n => T ≤ |E n|)).card : ℝ) ≤ (∑ n ∈ S, (E n) ^ 2) / T ^ 2 := by
  rw [ le_div_iff₀ ] <;> try positivity;
  convert chebyshev_inequality_finset S E T hT using 1

/-- **Level of distribution corollary.**
If the mean-square bound `∑ n ∈ S, (E n)² ≤ V` holds, then the exceptional set
`{n ∈ S : T ≤ |E n|}` has size at most `V / T²`. -/
theorem level_of_distribution_bound {α : Type*} (S : Finset α) (E : α → ℝ)
    (T V : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) (hV : ∑ n ∈ S, (E n) ^ 2 ≤ V) :
    ((S.filter (fun n => T ≤ |E n|)).card : ℝ) ≤ V / T ^ 2 := by
  convert chebyshev_card_le_div S E T hT |> le_trans <| ?_ using 1;
  gcongr

/-
**Goldbach instantiation.**
With threshold `T = X / (log X)^A` and mean-square bound
`∑ n ∈ S, (E n)² ≤ X³ / (log X)^{3A}`, the exceptional set has size at most
`X / (log X)^A`.
-/
theorem goldbach_exceptional_set_bound {α : Type*} (S : Finset α) (E : α → ℝ)
    (X A : ℝ) (hX : 0 < X) (hL : 1 < Real.log X)
    (hV : ∑ n ∈ S, (E n) ^ 2 ≤ X ^ 3 / (Real.log X) ^ (3 * A)) :
    ((S.filter (fun n => X / (Real.log X) ^ A ≤ |E n|)).card : ℝ)
      ≤ X / (Real.log X) ^ A := by
  convert level_of_distribution_bound S E ( X / Real.log X ^ A ) ( X ^ 3 / Real.log X ^ ( 3 * A ) ) ?_ hV using 1;
  · field_simp;
    rw [ ← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul ( by positivity ), mul_comm ] ; norm_num;
  · positivity

end ChebyshevExceptionalSet
